purpose: Close the consumer side of the cross-tenant read measured in #4839. On a live PostgreSQL 16 carrying all 182 forward-only migrations, under the application role app_runtime (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS) and with no RLS context set - which is exactly how ExportsService runs, since it takes PrismaService rather than rls-transaction.service - a deals read with no tenant predicate returned both tenants' rows. The cause is the policy deals_app_access USING (true): PostgreSQL combines permissive policies with OR, so it nullifies the strict deals_select. Five export reads had no tenant predicate at all; assertExportRole checked the role and nothing else, and user.tenantId never reached a query.
requiredInvariants: Five reads, not one. exportDealsCsv, exportRegulatoryReport, exportEvidenceBundle, exportLedgerCsv and exportDealReport all read deal-owned data and none carried a tenant predicate. Closing one and leaving four would repeat the defect this programme keeps finding.

A missing tenant is a refusal, not a wider read. If user.tenantId is absent the export throws rather than querying without a predicate - otherwise the exact read being closed would survive for any caller whose token lacks a tenant. Same fail-closed shape as postgresql-deal-command.service.ts.
Another tenant's deal is indistinguishable from a missing one: findFirst with the tenant predicate, never findUnique by id followed by a check.

The ledger keeps its ownership check even though RLS already returns nothing for it. ledger_entries has no tenant column, so ownership is established through the deal. Relying on 'the query returns nothing anyway' would be a control that holds because of an unrelated accident.
The role check still runs first, so a caller without an export role is refused for that reason rather than for the tenant.

deals_app_access is NOT touched. Closing that policy needs a deals_update policy and the deal command path exercised against it; it is recorded in #4814 and belongs to its own pass. Fixing RLS inside an export pass is the substitution this programme forbids.

V8.2.2 and V8.4.1 are NOT claimed and stay FAIL. This closes five consumers of a boundary that is still open; the boundary is the policy. Marking them PASS here would answer the requirement with the evidence of a narrower one - which is why the ASVS decisions file is not touched by this pass at all. The requirement id was corrected during the pass: the first version of this manifest cited V8.2.3, which is field-level access (BOPLA). A cross-tenant row read is V8.2.2 - 'data-specific access ... to mitigate BOLA' - and it is L1 rather than L2. V8.2.3's own recorded note warns it is the requirement most at risk of being answered with the wrong evidence, because row level security restricts which ROWS a consumer sees and says nothing about which FIELDS; citing it for a row read would have been exactly that error.

exportOutboxStatus is deliberately left alone and recorded: it reads the outbox queue with no tenant predicate and returns raw entries, but whether that queue is tenant-scoped at all is a semantic question rather than a missing predicate, and guessing would either break an infrastructure view or leave a false sense of closure.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no new dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Measured before fixing, on a live database rather than argued from reading: 182 migrations applied clean, app_runtime confirmed super=false bypassrls=false, and with no RLS context a deals read returned 2 rows across both tenants while a ledger read returned 0. The policy list confirmed deals_app_access | ALL | true alongside the strict deals_select.
exports-tenant-scope.spec.ts 11 of 11, covering all five reads plus the role-first ordering.

Four mutations, each caught: dropping the predicate from exportDealsCsv fails 1; dropping it from the regulatory report fails 1; going back to findUnique by id for the evidence bundle fails 1; and letting a missing tenant through instead of refusing fails 5 - the sharpest of them, because that is the shape the defect would take if the guard were softened later.

Not proven and not claimed: production grants. In a migration-only database app_runtime has no table privileges at all, so SELECT was granted by hand to test RLS specifically. Nothing is asserted about the production principal.

The regulatory report is called out separately because its rows leave the platform - they are filed to МСХ, Росстат, ФНС and Росфинмониторинг. A foreign tenant's deal there is not a wrong screen, it is a wrong filing.

Two pre-existing spec fixtures had to be corrected, and the question of which side was wrong was answered rather than assumed: exports-output-encoding.spec.ts and exports-content-disposition.spec.ts built an ADMIN with no tenantId, so seven tests failed once the tenant became mandatory. The platform's own deal command path (assertTrustedUser in postgresql-deal-command.service.ts) already refuses a user without tenantId, so those fixtures described a caller the system would reject anyway. The fixtures were made representative; the guard was not softened to fit them. exports + content-disposition 31 of 31.
